scenario.name: Microsoft & Kaspersky — Salt Typhoon (GhostEmperor): Demodex Rootkit & Telecom Core Capture
scenario.shortSubtitle: Microsoft Threat Intel / Kaspersky GReAT · BYOVD Demodex Kernel Rootkit & TACACS+ Capture
scenario.overview: Imagine a national telephone switching center whose exterior maintenance console gets compromised to mint a brand-new supreme-level supervisor badge. Rather than running noisy programs on the main switchboard where telecom engineers watch closely, the spy turns on a hidden built-in utility side room inside the switch itself to stash permanent tools, then silently clips wiretaps straight onto the trunk lines to capture core network passwords and ride deep into the national telecom backbone. In this scenario (T1014, Microsoft & Kaspersky, Salt Typhoon (GhostEmperor): Demodex Rootkit & Telecom Core Capture) on NOC-WIN-01 (10.30.1), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: compromising the Edge Router Web UI, then activating the Router’s Linux "Guest Shell", then sniffing Core TACACS+ / RADIUS Credentials. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Compromising the Edge Router Web UI, then Activating the Router’s Linux "Guest Shell", then Sniffing Core TACACS+ / RADIUS Credentials, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: BYOVD VULNERABLE SIGNED DRIVER LOAD (DSE BYPASS)
stages.subtitle: Abusing signed kernel driver IOCTL to bypass Windows Driver Signature Enforcement
stages.description: Entering through an exposed exterior switchboard web dashboard, the spy modifies the device's live configuration straight from the front panel to carve out a brand-new highest-privilege administrator account. From NOC jump host NOC-WIN-01 (10.30.1.10), with stolen data later staged toward C2 203.0.113.195:443, the attacker exploits an exposed management interface or captured configuration credential on a telecom edge router (such as the Cisco IOS XE Web UI / webui_wsma_http endpoint) to execute privileged configuration commands and create a hidden local user account with privilege 15 (in Cisco IOS XE, Privilege Level 15 is the highest "enable" administrative tier, granting unrestricted control over routing tables, packet capture, and system containers). Creating a local fallback account with username <name> privilege 15 secret <hash> allows the attacker to log directly into the router with full administrative authority whenever local authentication fallback is enabled or by bypassing centralized AAA checks. In the documented Sysmon EID 6 exchange from Salt Typhoon C2 Relay to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with ACK Event 6 (confirming that the BYOVD DRIVER LOAD request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 DEMODEX KERNEL ROOTKIT MINIFILTER & REGISTRY HIDING). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ BYOVD DRIVER LOAD / ⇠#1 ACK Event 6) from Node ① (#1 Salt Typhoon C2 Relay) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Defender XDR & Telecom NDR).

stages.title: DEMODEX KERNEL ROOTKIT MINIFILTER & REGISTRY HIDING
stages.subtitle: FltRegisterFilter and CmRegisterCallbackEx conceal implant artifacts
stages.description: Knowing that telecom engineers rarely inspect the switch's built-in utility closet, the spy switches on that hidden back room, attaches a private side corridor to it, and parks custom espionage tools safely away from ordinary switchboard inspections. Instead of dropping files onto the router’s standard flash storage (where any network engineer running "dir flash:" would immediately spot an unfamiliar file), the attacker enables iox (Cisco’s Application Hosting framework) and runs guestshell enable (which boots a built-in Linux container inside the router, originally designed by Cisco so engineers could run Python automation scripts, but abused by the attacker because processes and files inside the Linux Guest Shell are completely hidden from standard IOS CLI commands like "show processes"). Inside the Guest Shell Linux container, the attacker has a full bash environment with network access to the router’s interfaces, allowing them to compile and run custom C2 tunnels, SSH relays, and packet sniffers inside an isolated container where no traditional endpoint EDR agent can be installed. In the documented Kernel Pool Scan exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to Telecom NOC Jump Server, Telecom NOC Jump Server responds with ALERT 96 KB Ring-0 (confirming that the DEMODEX ROOTKIT request succeeded on Telecom NOC Jump Server and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 TELECOM TACACS+ CREDENTIAL CAPTURE & CORE ROUTER PIVOT). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ DEMODEX ROOTKIT / ⇠#2 ALERT 96 KB Ring-0) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Telecom NOC Jump Server), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Defender XDR & Telecom NDR).

stages.title: TELECOM TACACS+ CREDENTIAL CAPTURE & CORE ROUTER PIVOT
stages.subtitle: Sniffing AAA authentication traffic and pivoting to core ISP routers
stages.description: From inside the compromised edge switch, the spy turns on the switch's built-in traffic recorder to scoop up administrator passcodes crossing the trunk lines, builds secret shielded bypass pipes, and rides straight into the core carrier switching fabric. From inside the compromised router, the attacker activates Embedded Packet Capture (EPC, monitor capture, the router’s built-in traffic recording feature) or runs tcpdump inside Guest Shell to sniff management-plane traffic passing through the router. They intercept TACACS+ (TCP port 49) and RADIUS (UDP port 1812) authentication packets alongside weak/obfuscated Type-7 passwords in router configs (harvesting the credentials of senior telecom engineers so the attacker can log into core MPLS/BGP backbone routers as a legitimate administrator). Because core telecom routers sit at the intersection of administrative management networks and subscriber trunks, passive packet capture on the router itself harvests authentication secrets in transit without generating noisy port scans across the internal network. In the documented Suricata TACACS+/SSH exchange from Telecom NOC Jump Server to Demodex Kernel Rootkit (Ring-0), Demodex Kernel Rootkit (Ring-0) responds with ALERT TCP/49 & :22 (confirming that the CORE ROUTER PIVOT request succeeded on Demodex Kernel Rootkit (Ring-0) and completing the final execution objective of Microsoft & Kaspersky, Salt Typhoon (GhostEmperor): Demodex Rootkit & Telecom Core Capture). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ CORE ROUTER PIVOT / ⇠#3 ALERT TCP/49 & :22) from Node ③ (#3 Telecom NOC Jump Server) to Node ④ (#4 Demodex Kernel Rootkit (Ring-0)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Defender XDR & Telecom NDR).

detectionRule.title: Kernel Driver Loaded from Suspicious Temp Directory (BYOVD)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Suspicious Kernel Driver Load from Temp Folder
logsource:
  category: driver_load
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ImageLoaded|contains:
      - '\Windows\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Enable Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist (HVCI / Memory Integrity) to prevent BYOVD loaders from mapping unsigned kernel rootkits.

detectionRule.title: Kaspersky GReAT — GhostEmperor Demodex Kernel Rootkit
detectionRule.ruleCode:
rule GhostEmperor_SaltTyphoon_Demodex_Rootkit {
  meta:
    author = "Kaspersky GReAT / Microsoft Threat Intel"
    actor = "GhostEmperor / Salt Typhoon"
  strings:
    $api1 = "FltRegisterFilter" wide ascii
    $api2 = "CmRegisterCallbackEx" wide ascii
    $api3 = "IoCreateSymbolicLink" wide ascii
    $tag = { 44 6D 64 78 }
  condition:
    uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and 3 of them
}
detectionRule.mitigation: Enforce Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity (HVCI) and monitor Kernel Patch Protection / unbacked kernel callback addresses.

detectionRule.title: Unauthorized Packet Capture & Config Export on Core Router
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Cisco IOS-XR / XE Unauthorized Monitor Capture Command
logsource:
  product: cisco
  service: aaa
detection:
  selection:
    CmdSet|contains:
      - 'monitor capture'
      - 'show running-config'
      - 'law-intercept'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Migrate management plane authentication from legacy TACACS+ (MD5 obfuscation) to mutual TLS / SSH certificates with hardware security keys.
